minutes.headline: Select Board put a senior-tax-relief study, an old-primary landscape article and an APD override article on the warrant; Bright Farms TIF vote held.
minutes.summary: The board met with the new state representative, heard a Complete Streets sidewalk update, and ratified a COA van driver. It reviewed the Bright Farms TIF agreement but waited for town counsel's view on "material" before signing. It also reviewed the Greenleaf Botanicals host agreement draft, discussed senior tax relief and the draft warrant, and received a budget update and town manager and COVID reports.

what_happened.line: The Select Board put an architectural preservation district appeal article and an old primary school landscape design article on the town meeting warrant.
The board held its vote on the Bright Farms TIF agreement for a week while the town manager asks town counsel whether missing the job count is a material breach.
Acceptance of the Bright Farms land parcel was postponed until the TIF agreement is executed.
The board decided senior tax relief is not ready for annual town meeting; staff will gather data on senior homeowners and run scenarios.
The board ratified a Council on Aging van driver and approved a virtual outreach meeting for Greenleaf Botanicals, 4-0 with one member away.

why_it_matters: The warrant articles, including the landscape design amount still to be set, are what residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting.
Senior tax relief will not be on this year's warrant, and the Wakefield-style program discussed would shift its cost to other residential taxpayers, so any later proposal bears on tax bills.
The Bright Farms TIF turns on how counsel reads "material", which decides what happens if the project falls short of its job count.
watch_next: Town counsel's view on whether missing the job count is a material breach, and the board's deferred Bright Farms TIF vote, expected in a week.
The amount for the old primary school landscape design article and the final wording of the preservation district article.
